# Review: MOsu seek→cut refactor

Scope: the 7 named files only (upstream `osu/` not read, per instructions; no builds/tests run, per instructions). Line numbers from the current working tree.

## Checklist

**1. Concurrency — two cuts interleaving / cut while settle pending: NO.**
`cut()` fires only when `settleDelegate == null && FrameStablePlayback` (MosuSeekController.cs:219-264). A cut sets `FrameStablePlayback=false` (:309); the *next* frame's first branch (:222) schedules the settle that restores it (:229) — so consecutive cuts have a hard ≥2-frame gap, and a cut can never fire while `settleDelegate` is pending (outer guard :220). Concurrent `RequestSeek` calls coalesce into the single `pendingCut` slot (queueCut, :190-193) — last-write-wins, no queue. The only other writer of `FrameStablePlayback` is `SafeSeek` (break skip, DrawableMosuRuleset.cs:134-158) — see Finding 5.

**2. fwd/bwd/fwd state corruption: bookkeeping is sound; one heuristic hole.**
Diffing is by reference (`Except`/`Except`, no `Equals` overrides on `HitObject`), `inPlayfield` is reassigned after every cut (:306), and `cut()` always updates `lastSplicedList` immediately after writing the splice (:295-306), so the out-of-band-adoption check (:280-286) can't false-positive on the controller's own writes. False *negative*: a mod that **mutates** the live list in place (`Clear()`+`AddRange`) instead of replacing the reference evades the `ReferenceEquals` check → backward cuts splice from a stale `originalHitObjects` snapshot (Finding 9). Straddler semantics are deterministic (`StartTime >= t`, whole-object drop), so re-cutting the same region is repeatable. One unverifiable-from-here caveat: after a forward cut, pre-cut hits may still sit in `scoreProcessor.Statistics` while maxes are re-derived from the tail; the Visual scene empirically reaches results, so upstream `ApplyBeatmap` evidently reconciles — residual risk, not evidence of a bug.
